bibl.title: GLIM criteria for the diagnosis of malnutrition – A consensus report from the global clinical nutrition community
bibl.publisher: Journal of Cachexia Sarcopenia and Muscle

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: A DIAGNOSTIC DEFINITION CHOSEN BY BALLOT AND GIVEN AN EXPIRY DATE - the GLIM criteria for malnutrition, five criteria ranked by vote out of the eight competing tools already in use, requiring one phenotypic and one etiologic criterion, to be `re-considered every 3-5 years`
span.quote: A two‐step approach for the malnutrition diagnosis was selected, i.e., first screening to identify “at risk” status by the use of any validated screening tool, and second, assessment for diagnosis and grading the severity of malnutrition. The malnutrition criteria for consideration were retrieved from existing approaches for screening and assessment. Potential criteria were subjected to a ballot among the GLIM core and supporting working group members. The top five ranked criteria included three phenotypic criteria (weight loss, low body mass index, and reduced muscle mass) and two etiologic criteria (reduced food intake or assimilation, and inflammation or disease burden). To diagnose malnutrition at least one phenotypic criterion and one etiologic criterion should be present.

span.label: how to give malnutrition one diagnostic definition usable worldwide, when eight existing approaches disagree and `no single existing approach has secured broad global acceptance`
span.quote: Although malnutrition is a global concern associated with incremental morbidity, mortality, and cost, there has been a fundamental lack of consensus on diagnostic criteria for application in clinical settings. No single existing approach has secured broad global acceptance. 1 , 4 , 5 , 6 , 7 , 8 Our evolving understanding of the contributions of disease/inflammation may render some concepts of malnutrition in the current International Classifications of Diseases (ICD‐10) ( http://www.who.int/classifications/icd/en/ ) inconsistent with approaches or nomenclature that are currently used in clinical practice and research.

span.label: a two-step scheme - screen with any validated tool, then diagnose - with five balloted criteria split into phenotypic and etiologic, severity graded on the phenotypic side only, and four etiology-based diagnosis categories
span.quote: Weight loss, reduced BMI, and reduced muscle mass were categorized as phenotypic criteria, and reduced food intake/assimilation and disease burden/inflammation as etiologic criteria (Table 3 and Figure 1 ). For the diagnosis of malnutrition, GLIM recommends that the combination of at least one phenotypic criterion and one etiologic criterion is required (Table 3 and Figure 1 ). The selection of threshold values for the consensus diagnostic criteria was guided by review of existing approaches used in screening and assessment as was the selection of threshold values for severity grading described below (see Appendix). The selected threshold values for diagnosis of malnutrition are shown in Table 3 . While only the phenotypic criteria are proposed for the severity grading that follows, the inclusion of the etiologic criteria for malnutrition diagnosis is deemed a priority to guide appropriate intervention and anticipated outcomes.

span.quote: A two‐step approach for the malnutrition diagnosis was selected, i.e., first screening to identify “at risk” status by the use of any validated screening tool, and second, assessment for diagnosis and grading the severity of malnutrition. span.label: undernutrition as a syndrome with several partly independent markers, none sufficient alone, overlapping three neighbouring constructs - cachexia, sarcopenia and frailty - that the new definition declines to absorb
span.quote: Similarly, patients with cachexia will meet GLIM consensus criteria for malnutrition related to chronic disease with inflammation. Since there is concern that inclusion of cachexia with other disease‐related malnutrition conditions may diminish appreciation for some distinctive features of cachexia, there has been understandable hesitation by some to equate cachexia with this GLIM diagnosis category. The GLIM consensus criteria for malnutrition are therefore intended to be used in parallel with established concepts and nomenclature, including for example, those of cachexia, sarcopenia and frailty.

span.label: four global nutrition societies convened as GLIM in 2016; a survey of existing screening and assessment approaches; a formal ballot ranking candidate criteria; three years of face-to-face meetings, calls and email to consensus
span.term: four global nutrition societies convened as GLIM in 2016; a survey of existing screening and assessment approaches; a formal ballot ranking candidate criteria; three years of face-to-face meetings, calls and email to consensus
span.quote: A comprehensive survey of existing approaches used in screening and assessment of malnutrition was conducted to identify criteria worthy of consideration (Table 1 and the Appendix). It was recognized that these approaches incorporate multiple common criteria. For example, the presence of weight loss and disease burden or inflammation is common to most of them as is reduced food intake (Table 1 ).

span.label: **A DEFINITION CHOSEN BY BALLOT**: `The malnutrition criteria for consideration were RETRIEVED FROM EXISTING APPROACHES for screening and assessment. Potential criteria were SUBJECTED TO A BALLOT among the GLIM core and supporting working group members. THE TOP FIVE RANKED CRITERIA included three phenotypic criteria (weight loss, low body mass index, and reduced muscle mass) and two etiologic criteria.` **The candidates came from what was already in use and the cut was a vote count** - the corpus's other consensus papers vote on a proposal; this one ranks a field
span.quote: A two‐step approach for the malnutrition diagnosis was selected, i.e., first screening to identify “at risk” status by the use of any validated screening tool, and second, assessment for diagnosis and grading the severity of malnutrition. The malnutrition criteria for consideration were retrieved from existing approaches for screening and assessment. Potential criteria were subjected to a ballot among the GLIM core and supporting working group members. The top five ranked criteria included three phenotypic criteria (weight loss, low body mass index, and reduced muscle mass) and two etiologic criteria (reduced food intake or assimilation, and inflammation or disease burden). To diagnose malnutrition at least one phenotypic criterion and one etiologic criterion should be present.

span.label: **AND THE DEFINITION HAS AN EXPIRY DATE**: `THE DIAGNOSTIC CONSTRUCT SHOULD BE RE-CONSIDERED EVERY 3-5 YEARS.` Repeated in the conclusion - `The GLIM consensus should be RE-EVALUATED based upon review of new studies and advances in screening and assessment EVERY 3-5 YEARS.` **A definition that schedules its own replacement.** polman2011 revised the McDonald criteria three times without ever saying when the next revision was due; this one puts it in the abstract
span.quote: A consensus scheme for diagnosing malnutrition in adults in clinical settings on a global scale is proposed. Next steps are to secure further collaboration and endorsements from leading nutrition professional societies, to identify overlaps with syndromes like cachexia and sarcopenia, and to promote dissemination, validation studies, and feedback. The diagnostic construct should be re‐considered every 3–5 years.

span.label: **AND THE SAME DOCUMENT IS PUBLISHED THREE TIMES, `SUBSTANTIALLY THE SAME`**: `This article was FIRST CO-PUBLISHED in the journal Clinical Nutrition and in the Journal of Parenteral and Enteral Nutrition and is RE-PUBLISHED HERE. MINOR DIFFERENCES IN STYLE MAY APPEAR IN EACH PUBLICATION, BUT THE ARTICLE IS SUBSTANTIALLY THE SAME IN EACH JOURNAL.` **Three published copies of one criteria set, none of them authoritative over the others** - anyone citing `the GLIM criteria` is citing one of three documents and the citation cannot say which
span.quote: This article was first co‐published in the journal Clinical Nutrition and in the Journal of Parenteral and Enteral Nutrition and is re‐published here. Minor differences in style may appear in each publication, but the article is substantially the same in each journal.

span.label: **AND ONE CRITERION CARRIES A DIFFERENT THRESHOLD BY CONTINENT, ON PURPOSE**: `There is SUBSTANTIAL REGIONAL VARIATION in the use of low BMI ... NORTH AMERICAN GLIM REPRESENTATIVES INDICATED THAT LOW BMI IS SELDOM USED as a clinical malnutrition marker in those regions ... Since OTHER REGIONS OF THE WORLD currently make use of BMI as a criterion ..., THE GLIM CONSENSUS INCLUDES LOW BMI. Further research is however needed to secure CONSENSUS REFERENCE BMI DATA FOR ASIAN POPULATIONS.` The published table carries both: `<20 if <70 years` and `Asia: <18.5 if <70 years`. **The exact opposite trade from li2020**, which held one HbA1c threshold across all of China `TO ENABLE COMPARISON` although it `WAS SET FOR THE US POPULATION`
span.quote: There is substantial regional variation in the use of low BMI as a phenotypic criterion for malnutrition diagnosis. North American GLIM representatives indicated that low BMI is seldom used as a clinical malnutrition marker in those regions. The experience from the current American population is that people are often overweight or obese and would need to lose substantial weight before low BMI designation would occur. Since other regions of the world currently make use of BMI as a criterion for recognition of malnutrition, the GLIM consensus includes low BMI. Further research is however needed to secure consensus reference BMI data for Asian populations in clinical settings.

span.label: AND THE CRITERION WITH THE STRONGEST EVIDENCE HAS THE WEAKEST MEASUREMENT: `Reduced muscle mass is a phenotypic criterion WITH STRONG EVIDENCE to support its inclusion ... HOWEVER, THERE IS NOT CONSENSUS REGARDING HOW BEST TO MEASURE AND DEFINE REDUCED MUSCLE MASS, PARTICULARLY IN CLINICAL SETTINGS ... these methods are STILL NOT AVAILABLE IN MOST SETTINGS for nutritional assessment throughout the globe.` **Agreement that it matters and disagreement about how to see it** - so the criteria list a hierarchy of substitutes down to `calf or arm muscle circumference`
span.quote: Reduced muscle mass is a phenotypic criterion with strong evidence to support its inclusion in the GLIM consensus criteria. However, there is not consensus regarding how best to measure and define reduced muscle mass, particularly in clinical settings. Therefore, GLIM recommends measurement by dual‐energy absorptiometry or other validated body composition measures such as bioelectrical impedance, ultrasound, computed tomography or magnetic resonance imaging, but these methods are still not available in most settings for nutritional assessment throughout the globe.

span.label: AND THE CUT-OFFS FOR THAT CRITERION ARE BORROWED FROM THREE OTHER WORKING GROUPS: `GLIM REFERS TO RECOMMENDATIONS FROM THE EUROPEAN WORKING GROUP ON SARCOPENIA IN OLDER PEOPLE (EWGSOP) and from The Foundation of National Institute of Health (FNIH) initiative, and the ASIAN WORKING GROUP ON SARCOPENIA (AWGS). REFERENCE STANDARDS FOR MUSCLE MASS MAY WARRANT ADJUSTMENT FOR RACE AND SEX.` **A malnutrition definition importing its thresholds from the sarcopenia literature** - which is why the two constructs then have to be told apart in the discussion
span.quote: For the purpose of recommended cut‐off values for muscle mass reductions, GLIM refers to recommendations from the European Working Group on Sarcopenia in Older People (EWGSOP) 15 and from The Foundation of National Institute of Health (FNIH) initiative, 16 and the Asian Working Group on Sarcopenia (AWGS). Reference standards for muscle mass may warrant adjustment for race and sex. Additional research is warranted to establish general reference standards as well as for some specific populations, e.g. in Asia.

span.label: **AND THE NEW DEFINITION IS EXPLICITLY NOT REPLACING ITS NEIGHBOURS**: `patients with cachexia WILL MEET GLIM CONSENSUS CRITERIA for malnutrition related to chronic disease with inflammation. Since there is concern that inclusion of cachexia ... MAY DIMINISH APPRECIATION FOR SOME DISTINCTIVE FEATURES OF CACHEXIA, there has been understandable hesitation by some TO EQUATE CACHEXIA WITH THIS GLIM DIAGNOSIS CATEGORY. The GLIM consensus criteria for malnutrition are therefore INTENDED TO BE USED IN PARALLEL WITH ESTABLISHED CONCEPTS AND NOMENCLATURE, including ... CACHEXIA, SARCOPENIA AND FRAILTY.` **A definition that subsumes its neighbours extensionally and refuses to replace them nominally**
span.quote: Similarly, patients with cachexia will meet GLIM consensus criteria for malnutrition related to chronic disease with inflammation. Since there is concern that inclusion of cachexia with other disease‐related malnutrition conditions may diminish appreciation for some distinctive features of cachexia, there has been understandable hesitation by some to equate cachexia with this GLIM diagnosis category. The GLIM consensus criteria for malnutrition are therefore intended to be used in parallel with established concepts and nomenclature, including for example, those of cachexia, sarcopenia and frailty.

span.label: AND THE FIELD DEPARTS FROM ITS PARENT CLASSIFICATION DELIBERATELY: `WHILE ETIOLOGY HAS NOT GENERALLY BEEN INCLUDED IN CRITERIA SUPPORTING THE DIAGNOSIS OF MEDICAL CONDITIONS IN THE ICD CONSTRUCT, THE INCLUSION OF ETIOLOGY HAS BEEN WIDELY ADOPTED IN THE CLINICAL NUTRITION COMMUNITY because it serves to GUIDE APPROPRIATE INTERVENTIONS and expected outcomes.` **A discipline knowingly using a different kind of criterion from the classification it wants to be adopted into** - and the conclusion then asks WHO to take it into ICD-11
span.quote: The recommended GLIM approach encompasses both phenotypic and etiologic criteria for the diagnosis of malnutrition but uses only phenotypic criteria cut‐points to provide for severity grading. While etiology has not generally been included in criteria supporting the diagnosis of medical conditions in the ICD construct, the inclusion of etiology has been widely adopted in the clinical nutrition community because it serves to guide appropriate interventions and expected outcomes. For example, the presence of disease‐associated inflammatory response has potential for major impacts upon treatment approach and anticipated outcome.

span.label: AND THE REASON THAT MATTERS IS MONEY: `We will also seek to share the GLIM consensus recommendations with the World Health Organization in the context of the INTERNATIONAL CLASSIFICATION OF DISEASES REVISION PROCESS (ICD-11). THIS IS A HIGH PRIORITY SINCE THIS CLASSIFICATION SCHEME GUIDES CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS AND REIMBURSEMENT ACROSS MUCH OF THE WORLD.` **The stated destination of a definition is a payment system**, which is the clearest statement in the corpus of what adoption is actually for
span.quote: We will also seek to share the GLIM consensus recommendations with the World Health Organization in the context of the International Classification of Diseases revision process (ICD‐11). This is a high priority since this classification scheme guides clinical diagnosis and reimbursement across much of the world.

span.label: AND SEVERITY IS GRADED ON ONE HALF OF THE DEFINITION ONLY: `Weight loss, reduced BMI, and reduced muscle mass were categorized as PHENOTYPIC CRITERIA, and reduced food intake/assimilation and disease burden/inflammation as ETIOLOGIC CRITERIA ... WHILE ONLY THE PHENOTYPIC CRITERIA ARE PROPOSED FOR THE SEVERITY GRADING that follows, THE INCLUSION OF THE ETIOLOGIC CRITERIA for malnutrition diagnosis IS DEEMED A PRIORITY TO GUIDE APPROPRIATE INTERVENTION.` **One half decides whether, the other half decides what to do about it** - and only the first half is measured on a scale
span.quote: Weight loss, reduced BMI, and reduced muscle mass were categorized as phenotypic criteria, and reduced food intake/assimilation and disease burden/inflammation as etiologic criteria (Table 3 and Figure 1 ). For the diagnosis of malnutrition, GLIM recommends that the combination of at least one phenotypic criterion and one etiologic criterion is required (Table 3 and Figure 1 ). The selection of threshold values for the consensus diagnostic criteria was guided by review of existing approaches used in screening and assessment as was the selection of threshold values for severity grading described below (see Appendix). The selected threshold values for diagnosis of malnutrition are shown in Table 3 . While only the phenotypic criteria are proposed for the severity grading that follows, the inclusion of the etiologic criteria for malnutrition diagnosis is deemed a priority to guide appropriate intervention and anticipated outcomes.

span.label: AND THE VALIDATION IS SCHEDULED AFTER PUBLICATION: `AFTER THE LAUNCH of the GLIM consensus IT IS IMPORTANT THAT THE NUTRITION COMMUNITY USE THE CRITERIA both in prospective and retrospective cohort studies as well as clinical trials IN ORDER TO VALIDATE ITS RELEVANCE FOR CLINICAL PRACTICE. Next steps are to SECURE ENDORSEMENTS from leading nutrition professional societies and to promote dissemination, VALIDATION TESTING, and feedback.` **Endorsement and validation are listed as parallel next steps**, in that order
span.quote: After the launch of the GLIM consensus it is important that the nutrition community use the criteria both in prospective and retrospective cohort studies as well as clinical trials in order to validate its relevance for clinical practice. Next steps are to secure endorsements from leading nutrition professional societies and to promote dissemination, validation testing, and feedback.

span.label: **THE CRITERIA ARE PUBLISHED BEFORE THEY ARE VALIDATED, AND THE PAPER SAYS SO**: `AFTER THE LAUNCH of the GLIM consensus it is important that the nutrition community USE THE CRITERIA ... IN ORDER TO VALIDATE ITS RELEVANCE FOR CLINICAL PRACTICE.` The supporting evidence offered is that `each of them ALONE is able to predict adverse clinical outcomes` - which is evidence for the components, not for the conjunction that the definition actually requires
span.quote: After the launch of the GLIM consensus it is important that the nutrition community use the criteria both in prospective and retrospective cohort studies as well as clinical trials in order to validate its relevance for clinical practice. Next steps are to secure endorsements from leading nutrition professional societies and to promote dissemination, validation testing, and feedback.

span.label: AND THE MOST EVIDENCED CRITERION CANNOT BE MEASURED IN MOST PLACES: `GLIM recommends measurement by DUAL-ENERGY ABSORPTIOMETRY or other validated body composition measures ..., BUT THESE METHODS ARE STILL NOT AVAILABLE IN MOST SETTINGS for nutritional assessment throughout the globe. PHYSICAL EXAMINATION OR ANTHROPOMETRIC MEASURES of calf or arm muscle circumference are THEREFORE INCLUDED AS ALTERNATIVE MEASURES.` **A global definition has to be satisfiable with a tape measure**, and the alternatives are not equivalent to the recommended method
span.quote: Reduced muscle mass is a phenotypic criterion with strong evidence to support its inclusion in the GLIM consensus criteria. However, there is not consensus regarding how best to measure and define reduced muscle mass, particularly in clinical settings. Therefore, GLIM recommends measurement by dual‐energy absorptiometry or other validated body composition measures such as bioelectrical impedance, ultrasound, computed tomography or magnetic resonance imaging, but these methods are still not available in most settings for nutritional assessment throughout the globe.

span.label: AND ONE ETIOLOGIC CRITERION RESTS ON CLINICAL JUDGEMENT BY ADMISSION: `WHILE SEVERE INFLAMMATION IS GENERALLY EASY TO DISCERN, CLINICAL JUDGEMENT IS OFTEN REQUIRED TO RECOGNIZE THAT OF LESSER DEGREE. Supportive proxy measures ... can include laboratory indicators like serum C-reactive protein, albumin, or pre-albumin.` **The mild-to-moderate band - which covers most chronic disease - has no threshold at all**, only proxies described as supportive
span.quote: GLIM members recognized that disease burden/inflammation has become a widely accepted etiologic criterion in existing screening and assessment tools (Table 1 ). Clinical diagnosis provides a simple approach to recognition of severe, chronic or frequently recurrent inflammation. 1 , 2 , 19 For example, major infections, burns, trauma, and closed head injury are associated with acute inflammation of a severe degree. Indicators of inflammation may include fever, negative nitrogen balance, and elevated resting energy expenditure. Most chronic organ diseases, like congestive heart failure, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, rheumatoid arthritis, chronic kidney or liver disease and cancer, are associated with chronic or recurrent inflammation of a mild to moderate degree. While severe inflammation is generally easy to discern, clinical judgement is often required to recognize that of lesser degree.

span.label: AND THE THRESHOLDS WERE SELECTED BY REVIEW RATHER THAN DERIVED: `THE SELECTION OF THRESHOLD VALUES for the consensus diagnostic criteria WAS GUIDED BY REVIEW OF EXISTING APPROACHES used in screening and assessment as was the selection of threshold values for severity grading.` The appendix prints the eight source tools' cut-offs side by side; **the GLIM numbers are a synthesis of those, not a measurement**, and the paper does not claim otherwise

span.label: AND THE REGIONAL BMI THRESHOLD IS FLAGGED AS UNFINISHED IN THE SAME BREATH AS IT IS PUBLISHED: `FURTHER RESEARCH IS HOWEVER NEEDED TO SECURE CONSENSUS REFERENCE BMI DATA FOR ASIAN POPULATIONS IN CLINICAL SETTINGS` - while `Asia: <18.5 if <70 years, or <20 if >70 years` is already in the criteria table

The experience from the current American population is that people are often overweight or obese and would need to lose substantial weight before low BMI designation would occur. Further research is however needed to secure consensus reference BMI data for Asian populations in clinical settings.

span.label: Inflammation
span.quote: Inflammation contributes to malnutrition through associated anorexia and decreased food intake as well as altered metabolism with elevation of resting energy expenditure and increased muscle catabolism. Altered body composition manifests as a decrease in any marker of muscle mass (fat‐free mass, muscle mass index or body cell mass). Thus, malnutrition is associated with adverse functional and clinical outcomes.

Altered body composition manifests as a decrease in any marker of muscle mass (fat‐free mass, muscle mass index or body cell mass). span.label: The classification
span.quote: An etiology‐based diagnosis classification is endorsed by GLIM consistent with those suggested previously by the International Consensus Guideline Committee, 1 the AND/ASPEN Guidelines, 7 and the ESPEN Guidelines. The classification includes malnutrition related to chronic disease with inflammation, malnutrition related to chronic disease with minimal or no perceived inflammation, malnutrition related to acute disease or injury with severe inflammation, and malnutrition related to starvation including hunger/food shortage associated with socioeconomic or environmental factors (Table 5 ).

span.quote: There was strong consensus that the key first step in the evaluation of nutritional status is malnutrition risk screening to identify “at risk” status by the use of any validated screening tool 12 , 13 , 14 ; some of these tools are noted in Table 1 and the Appendix. span.quote: GLIM members recognized that disease burden/inflammation has become a widely accepted etiologic criterion in existing screening and assessment tools (Table 1 ). Clinical diagnosis provides a simple approach to recognition of severe, chronic or frequently recurrent inflammation. 1 , 2 , 19 For example, major infections, burns, trauma, and closed head injury are associated with acute inflammation of a severe degree. Indicators of inflammation may include fever, negative nitrogen balance, and elevated resting energy expenditure. Most chronic organ diseases, like congestive heart failure, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, rheumatoid arthritis, chronic kidney or liver disease and cancer, are associated with chronic or recurrent inflammation of a mild to moderate degree. While severe inflammation is generally easy to discern, clinical judgement is often required to recognize that of lesser degree.

span.quote: Assessment of muscle function using grip strength or other validated procedures is recommended as a supportive measure in the GLIM consensus (Tables 3 and 4 ). Decline in muscle strength generally exceeds changes in muscle size. 18 However, irrespective of etiology, appreciable loss of muscle mass is generally accompanied by reduced muscle function. In situations where muscle mass cannot be readily assessed then muscle strength, e.g. hand grip strength, is an appropriate supporting proxy.
